headline: Dec 4 terms: a verified email domain can see your account and public sites, and may absorb the account after notice
tldr: From Dec 4, an org that verifies your email's domain can see that your Netlify account exists, its plan, and your public sites' names, URLs and last deploy dates. If it also has a Netlify subscription, your account can move under its control unless you change your email in the notice window.
who: Anyone with a Netlify account whose email is on a company or school domain, especially personal projects signed up with a work email
seo_title: Netlify Dec 4 terms: verified domains can see staff accounts and may absorb them
seo_desc: Netlify's Nov 4 Self-Serve Subscription Agreement (effective Dec 4, 2026) adds Verified Domains (section 6.6) and restates account moves (section 2.1). Opt out of visibility at privacy@netlify.com.

redline.after: If Netlify verifies that an organization owns or controls the domain of the email address associated with Customer's account, Netlify may disclose to that organization the existence of Customer's account, its plan type, and information about the sites under that account that are publicly accessible on the Services, such as their site names, URLs, and when they were last deployed.
redline.label: Self-Serve Subscription Agreement · 6.6 Verified Domains (new)
redline.note: The Oct 1, 2025 agreement had no Verified Domains section. Domain visibility of account existence, plan and public sites is new.

redline.before: if the domain of the email address associated with your account is owned or controlled by an entity and Netlify has now or in the future a direct subscription agreement with such entity, your account may be rolled into and consolidated with that organization's account after notification to you. Following notice to you, if you choose not to change the email address associated with your account, your account will be controlled by the entity.
redline.after: If the domain of the email address associated with Customer's account is owned or controlled by an organization that has or later enters into a subscription agreement with Netlify, Customer's account may be consolidated into that organization's account after notice to Customer. If Customer does not change the email address associated with the account within the period stated in such notice, the account, including its Customer Content, will be controlled by that organization.
redline.label: Self-Serve Subscription Agreement · account moves (preamble → 2.1)
redline.note: Account absorption already existed in the Oct 1, 2025 preamble. The Nov 4 rewrite moves it into section 2.1, ties the deadline to the notice, and says Customer Content goes with the account.

redline.after: Verified Organizations: if your account uses an email address on a domain controlled by an organization that has verified that domain with us, we may show that organization's authorized administrators that your account exists, its plan type, and the names, URLs, and last deploy dates of your publicly accessible sites.
redline.label: Privacy Statement · 4. Disclosure of Personal Data (new category)
redline.note: The Privacy Statement (last updated Nov 4, 2026) adds Verified Organizations as a disclosure category and points opt-out to privacy@netlify.com.

actions: If you use a work or school email on Netlify for personal projects, change the account email to a personal address before Dec 4, or as soon as you get a move notice
To stop a verified organization seeing that your account exists, email privacy@netlify.com (Netlify's changelog and Privacy Statement both say this)
Read sections 2.1 and 6.6 of the Self-Serve Subscription Agreement PDF linked from netlify.com/changelog/updates-to-our-terms-and-privacy-statement/
If your organization already has an Enterprise Master Subscription Agreement with Netlify, that agreement still governs instead of the self-serve terms
what:
Netlify published a changelog on Nov 4, 2026 saying it updated its Self-Serve Subscription Agreement, Privacy Statement and Acceptable Use Policy, and that the changes take effect on December 4, 2026. We compared the live Self-Serve Subscription Agreement PDF (Last Updated: November 4, 2026) to the prior PDF archived by the Wayback Machine on Oct 16, 2026 (Last Updated: October 1, 2025), and read the live Privacy Statement (Last updated: November 4, 2026).

## Change 1: Verified Domains can see that your account exists

Section 6.6 is new. It is not in the October 1, 2025 agreement. The November 4 text says that if Netlify verifies that an organization owns or controls the domain of the email address on your account, Netlify may disclose to that organization "the existence of Customer's account, its plan type, and information about the sites under that account that are publicly accessible on the Services, such as their site names, URLs, and when they were last deployed."

The same section says Netlify will not, under 6.6, disclose payment information, or your name, email or username "other than as they may appear in any account names, site names, or URLs," and will not disclose Customer Content that is not publicly accessible. "Verification alone does not give that organization access to or control over Customer's account."

Netlify's own changelog puts the same point in plain English: an organization that proves the domain "may show it that your account exists, its plan type, and the names, URLs, and last deploy dates of your publicly accessible sites," and never shows your name, email, username or payment information that way.

## Change 2: Account moves are restated, with Customer Content named

The October 1, 2025 agreement already warned, in the preamble before section 1: if the domain of your account email is owned or controlled by an entity that has (or later gets) a direct subscription agreement with Netlify, "your account may be rolled into and consolidated with that organization's account after notification to you," and if you do not change the email, "your account will be controlled by the entity."

The November 4 agreement moves that rule into section 2.1 (Accounts and Email Addresses). It says the account "may be consolidated into that organization's account after notice to Customer." If you do not change the email "within the period stated in such notice, the account, including its Customer Content, will be controlled by that organization."

So Dec 4 is not the first day Netlify could absorb a domain-matched account. What is new for readers is the pairing with Verified Domains visibility, the notice-window wording, and the explicit line that Customer Content goes with the moved account.

## Change 3: Privacy Statement adds Verified Organizations and an opt-out

The Privacy Statement dated November 4, 2026 adds an "Organization domains" processing purpose that points to sections 6.6 and 2.1, and a "Verified Organizations" disclosure category with the same account-exists / plan / public-site fields. Section 8 says you can "Opt out of domain visibility at any time by contacting us at privacy@netlify.com," and that changing your account email to one outside the organization's domain before the date in a move notice stops the transfer. The changelog repeats both steps.

## What stays the same

Enterprise Master Subscription Agreement customers are still under that agreement, not this self-serve one. The November 4 agreement also keeps Netlify's line that it will not use Customer Content to train or fine-tune AI models unless the customer opts in.

## What you can do

Personal projects on a work email are the risk case. Change the email, or email privacy@netlify.com for visibility opt-out, and watch for any move notice after Dec 4.

Coverage (checked Nov 9, 2026): Netlify's own changelog is the announcement. The independent tracker toolongdidnotread.it flagged the Privacy Statement change. A Spanish-language blog (rubenloan.com) also covered it. We found no English-language news story from The Register, TechCrunch or similar on this Dec 4 update when we checked.
faq: Can my employer see my personal Netlify sites after December 4, 2026?

Only if it verifies ownership or control of the domain on your account email, and only for sites that are publicly accessible. Section 6.6 says Netlify may show account existence, plan type, and public site names, URLs and last deploy dates. It says verification alone does not give the organization access to or control over the account, and private or password-protected site content is not disclosed under 6.6.
Can Netlify move my account into my company's Netlify account?

Yes, if the domain of your account email is owned or controlled by an organization that has a subscription agreement with Netlify. Section 2.1 says Netlify will notify you first; if you do not change the email within the period in that notice, the organization controls the account and its Customer Content. A similar consolidation warning already appeared in the October 1, 2025 preamble.
How do I opt out of domain visibility?

Email privacy@netlify.com. Netlify's changelog and Privacy Statement both say that stops showing your account to verified organizations. Separately, change your account email to one outside the organization's domain before any move-notice deadline if you do not want the account absorbed.
When do the Netlify changes take effect?
December 4, 2026, per Netlify's Nov 4 changelog. The Self-Serve Subscription Agreement PDF and Privacy Statement are both marked Last Updated / last updated November 4, 2026.
Is Verified Domains brand new?

Yes in the self-serve agreement we compared. The October 1, 2025 PDF (Wayback capture Oct 16, 2026) has no section 6.6 and no disclosure of plan type or public site lists to a verified domain owner. Account consolidation for domain-matched emails did already exist in that older preamble.

headline: Dec 1: one account per person, and AI will analyze project content and editing history until you delete the account
tldr: From Dec 1, Vrew allows only one account per person (no team sharing on one login) and will use AI to analyze project content, assets and editing history for personalization, kept until the account is deleted. Object via chat support by Dec 1.
who: Vrew users who share a paid login across a team, or who keep project footage, captions and edit history they do not want AI-analyzed

seo_desc: Vrew's Dec 1 Terms and Privacy updates ban multi-account and shared logins, and add AI analysis of project content, assets and editing history until account deletion. Object via chat support by Dec 1.

If you disagree with the revised Terms, tell Vrew through Help → Support → Chat Support by Dec 1, or delete the account

Read Vrew's notice (and the linked current/revised Terms and Privacy pages) before Dec 1
what:
Vrew published a help article announcing updates to its Terms of Service and Privacy Policy effective December 1, 2026. The quotes below are from that notice's own current/revised comparison tables and retention table (fetched Nov 9, 2026). We are treating the vendor notice as the primary source for this due-soon item; we did not re-fetch every linked revised PDF beyond the notice.

## Change 1: One account per person, not per email

Vrew's notice says that starting December 1, "you may use only one account, even if you have different email addresses." Its table moves the rule from "The Service supports only one account per email address" (Article 5, Paragraph 1) to "Only one account is permitted per User for the Service" (Article 6, Paragraph 1).

It also says multiple people may not share one account, "including within companies and teams," and asks users to prepare separate accounts before December 1. Separately, Vrew says it is working on a company/team way to manage multiple accounts and will share details later.

## Change 2: AI analysis of project content and editing history

The Privacy Policy table replaces a footnote that said the company does not use project files for training and does not arbitrarily access or analyze project content without consent. The revised footnote says the company "analyzes the contents and assets of projects and the user's editing history using artificial intelligence" to provide a personalized editing experience, and "does not use the user's information for training artificial intelligence other than for this purpose."

A new processing row lists "Project categories, summaries, and assets; your editing history" for "Provision of personalized services," retained "Until you delete your account." The notice says analysis covers images, videos, audio and captions (assets), turned into topic categories and content summaries.

## What you can do

Object through in-app chat support by December 1, or delete the account. Vrew says that if you do not object by the effective date, it will treat that as agreement.

Coverage (checked Nov 9, 2026): We found no press coverage of the December 1 Vrew Terms/Privacy update beyond Vrew's own help article.
faq: Can my team keep sharing one Vrew account after December 1, 2026?

No, under the revised Terms described in Vrew's notice. It says multiple people may not share one account, including inside companies and teams, and asks each person to use their own account before December 1.
Will Vrew train generative AI on my project files?

Vrew's revised privacy footnote says it analyzes project contents, assets and editing history with AI for a personalized editing experience, and "does not use the user's information for training artificial intelligence other than for this purpose." That is narrower than open-ended training, but it is still AI analysis of your project material.
How long does Vrew keep the AI analysis?
The notice's retention table says project categories, summaries, assets and editing history for personalized services are kept until you delete your account.
How do I object?
Vrew says: in the app, Help → Support → Chat Support, by December 1, 2026. You can also delete the account. If you do not object by the effective date, Vrew says it will consider you to have agreed.

headline: Your cash back rate is now "personalized" and may differ from other members'
tldr: Rakuten's Oct 23 terms and privacy policy say cash back rates are personalized by your account history, shopping behavior and membership status, so your rate at a store may differ from another member's. Cash back is now "Rewards," with partner-point conversions and a $2,000-a-day gift card cap.
who: US Rakuten members who earn cash back through rakuten.com, the Rakuten app or the browser extension

what:
Rakuten (the cash back site formerly called Ebates) updated both its Terms & Conditions and its Privacy Policy on October 23, 2026. We compared the live terms (fetched Nov 9, 2026) with the previous version, dated October 15, 2025, as archived by the Wayback Machine on April 15, 2026. We compared the live privacy policy with the version dated December 18, 2025, archived July 12, 2026. Rakuten says it has more than 17 million members.

## Change 1: Your cash back rate is now "personalized"

The old terms described cash back as a cut of Rakuten's referral fee: "Rakuten gives a portion of this fee to its Members as Cash Back." They said cash back amounts "VARY BY AFFILIATE STORE AND PRODUCT CATEGORY."

The October 23 terms add a new sentence to Section 4: "Rewards rates and offers available through the Services are personalized and may vary by Member based on factors including your account history, shopping behavior, and membership status as described in our Privacy Policy. As a result, the Rewards rate available to you may differ from the rate available to other Members for the same Brand or product."

The exclusions section changes in the same way. "CASH BACK AMOUNTS VARY BY AFFILIATE STORE AND PRODUCT CATEGORY" becomes "REWARD AMOUNTS VARY BY BRAND, PRODUCT CATEGORY, BY MEMBER, AND BY SURFACE." The terms don't define "surface." Read plainly, it means the rate can also depend on where you see the offer (website, app, browser extension, or another channel).

The privacy policy now says it too. To its section on personalizing the service, Rakuten added: "The offers and cash back rates available to you may be personalized based on your account history, shopping behavior, and membership status, and may differ from those available to other members." The December 18, 2025 version only talked about personalizing which offers and stores you are shown, not your rate.

Neither document says what "membership status" means. The updated privacy policy does newly name one paid service, "Rakuten Plus," in its list of services that require payments.

## What Rakuten already told brands

Personalized rates are not new on Rakuten's business side. A May 14, 2024 post on Rakuten's site for brands describes "Personalized Rewards" as "tailor-made campaigns, designed to target brands' ideal audiences with a unique Cash Back rate," built on "shopper data such as brand preferences, interests, demographics, and conversion rates." It lists campaign types "including re-engagement, category affinity, and demographics targeting." In its example, a fashion brand offered new shoppers "a personalized, elevated 20% Cash Back rate, 3x the brand's typical base rate," and the post says "To ensure existing customers are not served the elevated Cash Back rate, brands have the option to layer in their own CRM data."

So the October 23 update puts in the member contract what Rakuten has pitched to brands since at least 2024: two members shopping the same store can be shown different rates. The terms don't say rates are ever lowered for anyone. They also no longer promise that everyone sees the same rate.

## Why this matters now

On October 28, 2026, five days after Rakuten's update, the FTC ordered nine companies (Delta, United, JetBlue, Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart, Walmart and Target) to explain whether prices vary "from one person to the next based on factors such as participation in loyalty programs or analysis of personal data," according to The Record. Rakuten is not one of the nine. But a cash back rate is part of what you actually pay, and Rakuten's contract now says yours is set partly from your shopping behavior.

## Other changes in the October 23 terms

**Cash back becomes "Rewards," and you can convert it to partner points.** Rewards now cover cash back, Bonuses and "Partner Points" (points or other currency from partners). If you convert cash back into Partner Points, they are "issued, valued, and administered by the applicable partner under that partner's terms, including any expiration, fees, or restrictions on use, and once converted they are no longer payable by Rakuten in U.S. dollars. Conversion may not be reversible."

**Gift card limits.** You can now redeem part of your balance as gift cards, but "Gift card redemptions are subject to a maximum of $2,000 per day." A new line says Rakuten "is not responsible for any gift card that is lost, stolen, expired, or otherwise unusable after delivery."

**Forfeiture now names confirmed rewards.** In the fraud and abuse section, "forfeiture of any accrued Cash Back rewards" becomes "forfeiture of any accrued or confirmed Rewards."

**More detail on how Rakuten is paid.** Section 4 now lists "referral or affiliate fees, marketing funds, cost-per-click or other performance-based fees, commissions on gift card redemptions, and other forms of consideration," and says Rakuten funds rewards from that money "and, for some offers, from its own funds."

## What stays the same

The $5 inactivity fee is not new. Both versions say that if you haven't shopped or started a shopping trip through Rakuten for more than 12 consecutive months, Rakuten "reserves the right to debit your Account balance five dollars ($5.00) per month" until you shop again or the balance hits zero. The arbitration clause and its 30-day opt-out (by signed letter, within 30 days of joining) are also the same; only the attention line on the mailing address changed.

## What you can do

Before you click through for a big purchase, compare the rate Rakuten shows you with the rate on other cash back portals or your card's shopping portal. Comparing what you see signed in with what a signed-out browser shows is a quick check, but it is not proof of how your own rate was set.

The privacy policy (in both versions) says that when Rakuten personalizes the offers you see from your tracked behavior "for the direct benefit of a particular merchant," that may count as "selling" or "sharing," and the Section 5 opt-out "would cover and remove you from this type of targeted marketing and personalization." Rakuten also says it honors Global Privacy Control signals. Opting out may also take you out of targeted higher rates, so it can cut both ways.

If you have a balance and rarely use Rakuten, cash it out (the minimum payout is still $5.01) so the $5-a-month inactivity fee can't eat it.

Coverage (checked Nov 9, 2026): We found no news story about the October 23 changes. An automated terms tracker (CrazyTOS) summarized the terms update; we found nothing on the privacy-policy line or on how it lines up with Rakuten's pitch to brands.
faq: Does Rakuten give everyone the same cash back rate?

Not according to its October 23, 2026 terms. They say rewards rates "are personalized and may vary by Member based on factors including your account history, shopping behavior, and membership status," and that your rate "may differ from the rate available to other Members for the same Brand or product."
When did Rakuten change its terms?
Both the Terms & Conditions and the Privacy Policy are marked "Updated: October 23, 2026." The previous terms were dated October 15, 2025 and the previous privacy policy December 18, 2025.
Is personalized cash back new at Rakuten?

Not on the business side. A May 2024 Rakuten post for brands describes "Personalized Rewards" campaigns that target audiences "with a unique Cash Back rate," including "demographics targeting," and says brands can keep existing customers from seeing an elevated rate. What's new is that the member terms and privacy policy now say so.
Can Rakuten lower my cash back rate because of my shopping history?

The terms don't say rates are lowered for anyone. They say rates can differ by member based on account history, shopping behavior and membership status, which means they no longer promise you'll see the same rate as other members.
Can I opt out of personalized Rakuten offers?

Partly. Rakuten's privacy policy says personalization based on your tracked behavior "for the direct benefit of a particular merchant" may count as selling or sharing, and its Section 5 opt-out "would cover and remove you from this type of targeted marketing and personalization." Rakuten also honors Global Privacy Control. Opting out may also remove targeted higher rates.
Does Rakuten charge an inactivity fee?

Yes, and that part is not new. If you haven't shopped or started a shopping trip through Rakuten for more than 12 consecutive months, it "reserves the right to debit your Account balance five dollars ($5.00) per month" until you shop again or the balance reaches zero. It won't make your balance negative.
Is there a limit on Rakuten gift card redemptions?
Yes. The October 23 terms say "Gift card redemptions are subject to a maximum of $2,000 per day," and you can now redeem part of your balance.
